category_title: Students with learning/speech disabilities who are on-task during active music-making but off-task during noninstructional transitions
minimal_context: The student is participating in Session 2 centers and is expected to wait their turn for a large group game with the teacher.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are starting Session 2 centers. Please sit here and wait your turn for the large group game with me.

STUDENT: (Turns away from the large group game and leans over to watch the other students playing the flash card game with a partner)

TUTOR: Please face forward and wait.

STUDENT: (Ignores the instruction and begins talking to the peers, becoming off-task during this noninstructional waiting time)

TUTOR: It will be your turn soon, just wait quietly.

STUDENT: (Gets up and walks away from the teacher entirely, demonstrating a high percentage of off-task behavior rather than waiting for their turn at the game)

options.A: Implement a specific termination stage counting down the final sessions of the center activities.
options.B: Give attention to the student's avoidance strategies as compensations rather than refusals to comply with the task.
options.C: Ask follow-up questions to model conversational skills during the center activities and waiting periods.
options.D: Maximize the time the student is engaged in active game-playing experiences during the centers.
